policy: Instructional visuals are continuously editable and expandable. This registry does not impose a maximum asset count.

assets.title: Hazard Control and Escalation Decision Flow
assets.purpose: Teach the boundary between routine control, stop/isolate, escalation, and emergency response.
assets.altText: Flowchart showing a technician observing a hazard, checking for an authorized routine control, applying and verifying that control when permitted, or stopping, isolating where authorized, and escalating when the task cannot proceed safely. Life-safety alarms direct the worker to the posted emergency procedure.

assets.title: PPE and Hazard Communication Information Map
assets.purpose: Show how task, hazard assessment, label/SDS information, site procedures, and restrictions combine before PPE and work authorization are confirmed.
assets.altText: Diagram linking the assigned task, employer hazard assessment, product label and Safety Data Sheet, and applicable restrictions to the current SOP or work-order decision and required PPE.

assets.title: Cultivation Work-Area Hazard Scan
assets.purpose: Give learners a visual workplace scan containing multiple hazard categories without implying the same risk level in every facility.
assets.altText: Simplified cultivation room showing irrigation water approaching damaged electrical equipment, a blocked aisle, an unstable ladder, an exposed cutting tool, high-intensity lighting, and a carbon-dioxide life-safety alarm, with a reminder to scan for other task-specific exposures.

assets.title: Biosecurity Pathway Map
assets.purpose: Map worker, tool, cart, hose, plant, debris, and zone-transition contamination pathways and reinforce controlled movement across boundaries.
assets.altText: Cultivation facility pathway diagram showing a cleaner or sensitive zone, a controlled transition boundary, and a higher-risk or unresolved zone connected by workers, tools, carts, hose ends, incoming materials, and waste movement. It emphasizes controlled sanitation before crossing and avoiding unnecessary backward travel.

assets.title: Cleaning Before Disinfection Sequence
assets.purpose: Show debris removal, cleaning, approved disinfection, verification, and documentation in a controlled sequence.
assets.altText: Nine-step sanitation workflow showing secure or remove material, remove debris and gross soil, physically clean, verify the approved product and preparation, apply as directed, maintain required contact conditions, complete the required finish step, inspect the result, and document completion or exceptions.

assets.title: Quarantine, Hold, and Restricted-Entry Comparison
assets.purpose: Differentiate plant-health quarantine, operational hold status, and pesticide restricted-entry requirements without collapsing distinct control systems.
assets.altText: Three-column comparison showing quarantine as separation for unresolved biological risk, hold as a status preventing movement or use pending an authorized decision, and pesticide restricted entry as a separate label-based worker-protection restriction. It notes that the statuses can coexist and do not cancel one another.

assets.title: Controlled Document Anatomy
assets.purpose: Annotate document ID, revision, effective status, prerequisites, sequence, acceptance criteria, records, and escalation.

assets.title: Material Genealogy Through Cultivation
assets.purpose: Show source plant or lot through movement, harvest container, sample, and disposition.

assets.title: Inventory Reconciliation Flow
assets.purpose: Show physical count, record count, verification, discrepancy preservation, and escalation.

assets.title: Operator Care Versus Servicing Boundary
assets.purpose: Differentiate normal operator checks and care from repairs or hazardous-energy servicing outside Technician I authority.

assets.title: Maintenance-Ready Fault Report
assets.purpose: Annotate observation, permitted check, result, impact, uncertainty, and escalation details.

assets.title: Professional Shift Handoff Model
assets.purpose: Show outgoing preparation, written record, two-way exchange, incoming cross-check, and ownership of open conditions.
